proposals: DGCI&S should publish each year a price-and-volume decomposition of the change in India’s import bill for crude oil, gold and the other principal commodities, so how much of the rise from $393 billion to $775.7 billion reflects paying more for the same barrel or gram, rather than buying more, is an official figure.

The RBI should include in each Monetary Policy Report an estimate of the contribution of imported crude and gold prices to headline CPI and WPI inflation, so the share of inflation that interest rates can do little about is quantified rather than argued in general terms.

The RBI should publish, for each financial year, a breakdown of the change in foreign exchange reserves into net intervention, valuation effects and other flows, so a $50.8 billion net dollar sale and a roughly $28 billion fall from peak reserves can be reconciled by readers.
